Entry.CreatedBy: Codex fresh f001 lane A evidence-first

AlternateTargets: three mysteries and three vital points

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Linji-house records use this paired label for a verbal device that a single phrase or shout is said to contain, and later teachers enumerate, test, or tell hearers to discard it.
EvidenceBody: Fenyang Shanzhao says that one phrase contains the three mysteries and three essentials, with guest and host clearly distinguished; his verse also calls them difficult to distinguish and turns from words to their intended point. Huiyan Zhizhao says that one shout encompasses them.

Tianyin Yuanxiu identifies the device with Linji and simultaneous illumination and function. Qiran Chaozhi asks which phrase is the three-mysteries-and-three-essentials phrase and elsewhere tells hearers to remove it together with other Linji-house arrangements. Jie'an Wujin lists it among the devices marking the Linji family.

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses across five independent works support one Linji-house device; component formulas are family controls, not extra exact-headword sources.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A Linji-house phrase device is said to be contained in one phrase or shout and is later tested alongside other house arrangements.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The witnesses do not supply one stable shared item-by-item taxonomy; a later component enumeration therefore does not license an invented universal list.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All exact witnesses present the same paired Linji-house label in different deployments, not distinct lexical senses.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases preserve the paired terms and Linji association while avoiding an unsupported itemized taxonomy.

ModifierControls.Finding: Both threes belong to the fixed paired label; they do not establish a stable six-item inventory across witnesses.

FamilyControls.Term: 一句語須具三玄門，一玄門須具三要
